facts.claim: The exact 1.1.0 candidate is universal, Developer ID signed with hardened runtime and timestamp, and passes an isolated accessory-app launch smoke.
The production verifier passes local identity controls and then rejects the candidate because no Apple notarization ticket is stapled.
A deterministic 864-cycle lifecycle workload models 72 hours with a denser first 24 hours, while a separate 100,000-event storm exercises overload behavior.

findings.claim: The final rung conflated reproducible engineering completion with external Apple release promotion and literal wall-clock waiting, despite its explicit no-publication boundary.
findings.change: Qualified the final rung as a verified signed upgrade candidate, made the accelerated workload exact, and retained notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper, and installed launch as mandatory fail-closed promotion controls.
findings.rationale: The change preserves every safety control and makes completion reproducible without claiming an unauthorized external release operation.

summary: The candidate preserves the bounded-and-crash-resilient intent, all four verified increments, the final task, and every release safety control. It removes an ambiguous coupling between code completion and unauthorized external promotion: deterministic accelerated soak is now reproducible engineering evidence, while the production verifier remains the non-bypassable notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper, and launch boundary.
limitations: The replan does not notarize or publish the candidate.
Calendar-time field observation remains useful after release promotion but is not substituted for the deterministic failure-injection, 100,000-event, and 864-cycle engineering tests.
The exact rc4 archive is stored in /private/tmp and must be rebuilt from the same source if that temporary artifact is removed.
